newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen opening just lower, heading for new peak.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen opening just lower, heading for new peak.

text.p: U.S. stocks could be mildly lower at Tuesday's opening due to profit-taking but are likely to shake off the selling and reach for new all-time highs.

"I suspect we'll see some profit-taking on the opening after yesterday's rally. ITT could also be a drag on the market initially, but then I expect a reversal," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
On Monday, the Dow rose 74 points to 5734, as investors grew more confident about interest rates and third-quarter corporate profits.
The rise put the index within a stone's throw of its record-high 5778 set on May 22.

"Profit-taking is showing up in London, but I expect this blue chip extravaganza to continue," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "Markets around the globe are strong, following the Dow. We've got the old mo(mentum) going for us and that could continue."

Tokyo stocks followed the Dow up, ending sharply higher and London stocks were trading higher at midday and the FTSE 100 set new all-time highs in London in late morning trading, then later slipped mildly on profit-taking.

"With no major economic news today, and as long as bonds hold their gains, we may have an attempt at the old highs. Tecnically the market is quite strong. And the dollar is supporting bonds," said Cardillo.

Wachtel noted the strength was shown in larger companies, driving up the Dow and the S&P 500 but leaving the Nasdaq and Russell 2000 trailing. He also said light volume could be aiding the blue-chip rise.
After the bell Monday, ITT said its third quarter profits would be disappointing on weak August revenues in parts of its gaming business, mostly in Las Vegas.
Standard & Poor's September futures were off 0.6 to 664.45 ahead of the New York opening.
The dollar clung to gains against both the mark and the yen, but could not break through resistance levels.

The initial public offering of Gulfstream Aerospace may not be able to get off the ground, according to the "Heard on the Street" column of the Wall Street Journal.
